result.label: ChatThread
result.title: How does risk-rules get its rules? (config load)
result.author: Arjun Mehta
result.text:
[2025-08-10 22:37] Priya Nair: Arjun, quick one while I go through the INC-2025-031 action items: where does risk-rules actually read rules from at request time?
[2025-08-10 22:40] Arjun Mehta: Not from its own DB on the hot path. rules-store-db is just the source of truth for the rule editor. On every cache miss risk-rules polls config-service's internal /v1/rulesets endpoint.
[2025-08-10 22:41] Arjun Mehta: It's not in the service catalog because it started as a "temporary" hack two years ago and nobody ever went back to register it.
[2025-08-10 22:43] Priya Nair: So if the rules cache is cold, every fraud-scoring call can fan out to config-service?
[2025-08-10 22:44] Arjun Mehta: Yes. Cold cache or tiny TTL, same thing: every payment turns into a rulesets fetch.
[2025-08-10 22:46] Priya Nair: That explains why config-service CPU was pinned during the incident. 10s TTL times ~40 pods at peak...
[2025-08-10 22:47] Arjun Mehta: Exactly. Every pod refetched the full ruleset every few seconds, all at once.
[2025-08-10 22:49] Priya Nair: Can we write a floor for that TTL down somewhere people will actually see it?
[2025-08-10 22:51] Arjun Mehta: Decision: RULES_CACHE_TTL stays at 300s minimum. Below ~30s config-service falls over at checkout peak — that's what bit us in INC-2025-031.
[2025-08-10 22:52] Priya Nair: Agreed. Please don't leave it only in Slack.
[2025-08-10 22:53] Arjun Mehta: I'll put it in the risk-rules README next sprint.
